verdict.rationale: Yapily's authorisation flows send users to their bank's own login screen, and its hosted flow handles SCA and bank redirects automatically. That is a bank-hosted consent model rather than credential scraping. However, it also documents an embedded authorisation flow for some institutions, and nothing in the pack documents per-institution OAuth/redirect coverage or any plan to retire credential-based or embedded flows. missing for 10: documented OAuth/redirect coverage list across major institutions, documentation of legacy/embedded credential flow retirement, explicit statement that no screen-scraping is used, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, connections to major institutions use bank-hosted OAuth rather than screen-scraped credentials — the platform documents its OAuth coverage and how legacy credential flows are being retired

citations.quote: Used to initiate the authorisation process and direct users to the login screen of their financial Institution in order to give their consent for a bulk payment.
Handles Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) and bank redirects automatically
